entities.summary:
The International Telecommunication Union (ITU) is a specialized agency of the United Nations for information and communication technologies, headquartered in Geneva. Founded in 1865, it was established to address the growing needs of the telegraph industry and its impact on global communication.

The ITU played a pivotal role in shaping the modern telecommunications landscape, establishing international standards for radio and satellite communications, and facilitating the development of the internet.

The ITU's legacy can be seen in the widespread adoption of digital technologies, the creation of the World Wide Web, and the establishment of the Internet Corporation for Assigned Names and Numbers (ICANN).

The ITU's work has also had a profound impact on the environment, with the agency helping to establish guidelines for the responsible use of radio frequencies and promoting sustainable practices in the telecommunications industry.

In 2016, the ITU launched its 5G Innovation Forum, which aims to accelerate the development and deployment of 5G networks and promote their use in the public sector.

As the ITU continues to evolve, it remains committed to its core mission of promoting international cooperation and coordination in the fields of telecommunications and information and communication technologies.
